author: reek
body: Pins the two operations the catalog was missing: row-set-by-name and catalog-update-row.

author: reek
body: The row count is the assertion that matters. An update has to REPLACE the row, and the way this was written everywhere before was query, set the field, insert the result -- which leaves the original in place and quietly gives you two rows with the same id. Reading the updated value back does not catch that, because a scan finds the new row either way. Counting does.

author: reek
body: The by-name setter also has to leave an unknown column alone rather than writing somewhere. That is the last line.

author: reek
body: `source row after set` is not a nicety, it is the surprise. row-set builds a fresh RowData and looks pure, but it fills it with `list-set-at (row.values) ...`, and list-set-at writes in place. So the row you passed IN changes too: the line prints grace, not ada, and any caller still holding the original is holding the new value. This is older than row-set-by-name and is not fixed here, because the fix is either a copy on every set or a change to list-set-at, and both are decisions with a cost. It is pinned so that whoever makes that decision finds the behaviour written down instead of discovering it.
